span.p: Interview Response Framework for Write-Through Design

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
9. Scale Considerations
Multi-region:
active-passive or
active-active with CRDTs.
Horizontal sharding:
consistent hashing. Global
consistency: write
coordinator with
consensus.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 450px; text-align: center;

span.p:
5. Walk Through Read Path
App reads key → Cache hit
(guaranteed fresh) →
Return data.
No DB round-trip needed
for written keys.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 450px; text-align: center;

span.p:
6. Discuss Failure Modes
DB failure: cache rollback
+ error. Cache crash: WAL
recovery. Network
partition: CP vs AP
choice. Concurrent writes:
version locking. Deadlock:
lock ordering, timeouts.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 450px; text-align: center;

span.p:
7. Analyze Trade-offs
Benefit: Strong cache
consistency,
read-your-writes, no stale
data. Cost: Write latency
(DB round-trip), lower
write throughput, write
amplification.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 450px; text-align: center;

span.p:
8. Propose Optimizations
Batched DB writes,
connection pooling,
WAL-backed recovery,
adaptive buffer sizing,
runtime consistency
checks.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 450px; text-align: center;

span.p:
1. Clarify Requirements
What data? Read-to-write
ratio? Consistency needs?
Latency SLA? Scale (users,
QPS, data volume)?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 450px; text-align: center;

span.p:
2. Define Scope
Write-through for which
operations? Anything that
doesn't need strong
consistency can use a
different strategy.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 450px; text-align: center;

span.p:
3. Propose Architecture
Draw: App → Write-Through
Cache → DB (primary +
replicas)
Label: components, data
flow, protocols

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 450px; text-align: center;

span.p:
4. Walk Through Write Path
App issues write → Cache
receives → Updates
internal state → Initiates
DB write → DB commits → DB
acknowledges → Cache
acknowledges app → Done
